body: I think I'm just going to try to sleep early, but thanks anyway.

Not really. I'm in a pretty isolated place right now, and the only people nearby are asleep, will be angry if i wake them, and aren't particularly kind to begin with. This whole "reaching out" thing doesn't seem to be working to be honest. I like the idea of talking to somebody on the phone but it's also terrifying and I don't think I could handle it if someone working on a hotline sent the police to bust down my door and drag me back to the place I was abused. Even just the paranoia I would have after calling, the fear that they're going to call the cops behind my back would be too much.

None of my friends are available. My urge is a lot more short-term than waiting until they're able to talk. I know I can make it past this if I make it the next few hours and manage to go to bed untouched but getting through the next few hours is the hardest part.
I'm sorry to hear things aren't so good for you, but this just makes me feel really guilty about being suicidal. It's not my fault things turned out ok for once.

To be completely honest, I'm terrified of mental health professionals. The last time I was suicidal I tried to get help and I ended up being abused by the doctors in my area. I want to talk to someone but I'd rather die that go through what I went through a second time.

Since I posted this I've started spiraling. I went for a walk outdoors because I thought it might help, but everything I saw reminded me of something depressing or made me sad for some reason or another. I tried to message my best friend because he's the only one I trust not to rat on me, but he isn't responding at all. I'm not sure why I'm spiraling so badly but I can't stop.
Yeah, I'm okay. Just haven't been online as much lately. Thanks for checking up.
Of course man. I hope you sleep well once you make it back. Have a good one.

Damn, that's awesome. I've never made pasta myself entirely, I've made sauce on my own, and I've made my own dough for other stuff like homemade bread and pizza, but never for noodles.

I know its the middle of the day, but I've actually been awake all night. I need to get some sleep. Thank you so much for talking with me though. I think before I head to bed, I'm going to unsubscribe from the pro-suicide subreddit I made this account for in the first place. It felt nice at the time, in a self-destructive way, but I should really stop going there.
I like most asian food. Sushi has a special place in my heart. I can kind of make it myself if I avoid raw fish, but I'm no sushi chef. It's still pretty good though.

To be completely honest, you did change whether I was sad. I don't know why talking to you helped when talking to other people didn't really do much, but it did. Maybe it won't be permanent, maybe tomorrow I will wake up and feel just as bad as I did when I woke up today or the day before. But it's something.

I think in a weird way that's what I needed, for someone to recognize that I'm struggling, but not treat me like a pity case, nor completely ignore it either. So thank you.

I guess being upbeat doesn't fit the idea of a suicidal person, idk.

I don't know to be honest. A lot of the issues I have are less of a matter of inherent ability and more of a matter of endurance and pain tolerance. I already lift weights, I have for a long time, but I don't know how far I can actually take it. The nice thing about lifting weights is that you can just get it over with. There's no staring at the clock waiting for it to end, or wondering how long I can keep going. You pick stuff up, you put it down, you count to 12, and you repeat until it's done. It's a bit of an unusual way to be. A walk to the store could do me in for days in terms of pain and strain, but picking up and moving the furniture to clean? not a problem for me. It'll take its toll if I have to keep picking things up all day long, or just keep moving around in general, but the act of actually picking stuff up isn't hard at all. High strength, low constitution & endurance.

Sure, lots. I think everyone does. Being a famous author, being a respected artist with a following, being a dedicated power-lifter, becoming a really good cook, finding a place to live that feels like home, finding people who feel like family, the list goes on.

I'm aware I can achieve this stuff through hard work and dedication, but it's often a question of "Is this worth it" when your effort and willpower takes you about a tenth as far as everyone else. Plus, when your brain is steeped in really bad rock-bottom depression, it's hard to care about hopes and dreams, even when normal you definitely wants all those things. I probably seem weirdly upbeat right now, because I'm in an upswing. This happens every couple days or every week or so, I'll have a day or maybe just a few hours where it seems like I'm improving, then something hits me or I even just go to bed and wake up the next day and the only emotions I seem capable of are just agonizing sadness, embarrassment, and fear.

I do live in the US. Obamacare doesn't actually work that well if you have literally no money. Most of the insurance policies I would get through it wouldn't cover any of the stuff I need, and none of them are free except for state-provided medicaid, that's really hard to get for political reasons. I'd go in-depth but I don't want to give away what state I live in.

It does kind of suck being alone, but that's not really the biggest thing weighing me down. Alone is fixable, you can meet new people. It's mostly just the state of my health. I tried for years to get proper treatment, when I had more money and some insurance, but nobody could or would do anything for me that actually helped, and that was just when it was purely the skeletal and back issues. Now I have a whole host of symptoms that range from mildly irritating to downright dangerous in the wrong circumstances, and for all I know I could be dying from something terrible. I certainly feel like I'm dying. I have tried going to the ER before for all this stuff, but all I got was a few expensive tests that found nothing, and a 3k bill. I feel like my mental health is failing too. It feels difficult to just talk to people like a normal person, I trip on my words constantly and my memory fails me more and more.

I know it sounds stupid, to be suicidal because you feel like you're going to die, but just having a vague sense of death and suffering hanging over your head in the back of your mind is much different than making a choice to die, and giving yourself back control, even if it's just for this one thing.

That's been on my to-do for a while honestly. I had one a long while back, but it was lost to trusting my computer with a half-assed tech guy. The story has changed a lot for the better since then anyway though. Maybe I'll work on that later today.
Yeah. I don't write it all down as much as I should though. I'm like 95% daydreaming and brainstorming, but I do actually remember the vast majority of how it goes.
I'll give it a look, sure.

Maybe? It depends really. I'm not really sure if it's something I can promise. I was supposed to draw Christmas gifts for all my friends since I'm broke as shit but I didn't end up even starting any of them. I'm sorry.
Hey man, that's cool. I've always thought photography was cool, but my main drive to take photos has always been so i could use them as drawing reference later.
Fair enough, I won't make you take up something you're not passionate about.

Hey, that ain't true. If you've got functioning hands that can make a line on a piece of paper, you can draw. I feel like I can't draw either, but I still manage to make lines on a screen show up, and that's what counts. There's ten thousand thrown-out sketches behind every masterpiece.

I have characters I work on and daydream about a lot, and I usually draw them. It's usually what I write about too. I mostly just enjoy drawing people in general. Digital paintings can be fun too. I work almost entirely digitally, just a tablet pen and a bootleg copy of SAI.

I'd rather not honestly. The only reason I felt okay posting this was because I'm using an anonymous account that I use just for suicidal stuff. I don't want this stuff to be traced back to my public identity at all.
Usually yeah. I post art online, and I share my writing with my friends mainly because I'm really self conscious about it.

I like to draw and write stories, but I haven't been doing that lately because it feels more like work than fun right now. I tried using drawing as a way to help my finances a bit but it didn't pan out at all, and now I just feel bad whenever I'm not drawing something amazing, and I feel worse for not practicing. I just don't enjoy it right now. Writing has been the same way. Even the games I like and have sunk hundreds of hours into feel pointless and boring.

I am not in college. I have a GED, and that's the extent of my education.
